text:
mike_h: Heads up — I've been tracking a slow-but-steady rise in corrected ECC and remap events on pool18/card5 over the last 48h. Not a hard spike but persistent growth.
leila_z: ack, what's the metrics trend? sudden or creeping?
anatoly_r: creeping. here's the short window from our telemetry (last 72h):
```
> 2026-03-15T02:00Z pool18/card5 ECC_CORRECTED=42 ROW_REMAP=3 PAGE_RETIRE=0
> 2026-03-16T02:00Z pool18/card5 ECC_CORRECTED=68 ROW_REMAP=7 PAGE_RETIRE=1
> 2026-03-17T02:00Z pool18/card5 ECC_CORRECTED=121 ROW_REMAP=14 PAGE_RETIRE=2
```
mike_h: row remap and page retire both incrementing — that's the pattern we've seen before when a row starts failing intermittently. Not yet Xid100s or reboots.
leila_z: any running noisy tenants on that card? might be memory pressure + hot pages.
anatoly_r: checked allocation: mostly steady, a couple of long-lived transformer jobs pinned to the card. I dumped kernel logs and saw repeated firmware-corrected ECC messages (no machine panic). sample dmesg: 
```
GPU0: ecc_corrected at 0x1fa3c (row 12345)
GPU0: row remap triggered, remap_count=1
GPU0: page retire scheduled (soft) page=0x7fffa3b000
```
sre_oncall_bot: incident-detect: page-retire-soft triggered on pool18/card5 at 2026-03-17T04:12Z. Not auto-evicting.
mike_h: Suggestion: quiesce long-lived jobs on card5 during next low-traffic window and trigger a controlled drain so we can observe any further remaps without impacting prod. If remap rate continues to climb, replace the card.
leila_z: agree. Also let's snapshot the KV cache evictions and latency around the drain window to confirm no customer impact. Can infra-bot schedule a drain candidate?
infra-bot: scheduling proposal: drain window 2026-03-18 03:00-05:00 UTC, target 2h. Will cordon card5, migrate pods, and watch remap counters. Reply with `:thumbsup:` to accept.
anatoly_r: +1. During the drain we should enable verbose telemetry and log the full row-remap trace (avoid sampling). Add `--telemetry=verbose --retain-logs=72h` to the runbook steps.
mike_h: runbook checklist (short):
1) mark card5 drain-safe: `fleetctl cordon gpu://pool18/card5`
2) migrate pinned jobs: `fleetctl migrate --from gpu://pool18/card5 --policy=graceful`
3) enable verbose telemetry on that host
4) monitor ECC_CORRECTED, ROW_REMAP, PAGE_RETIRE, and Xid errors every 5m
5) if ROW_REMAP > 20 or PAGE_RETIRE increments > 3 in-window -> escalate to RMA

leila_z: can we do a quick capacity impact estimate? pool18 currently has 64 cards with 4 spareable. Losing card5 temporarily will reduce headroom by ~1.6%. However if migration concentrates load on 3 nearby cards may see local tail latency.
anatoly_r: I'll pre-warm migrations to avoid bursty placement. Also add placement constraint to avoid stacking on same NUMA region.
sre_oncall_bot: note: previous similar pattern (pool7-card3) required replacement after 4 weeks of creeping ECC. If we see similar slope, we should plan replacement logistics (spare allocation + RMA ticket).
mike_h: okay, plan: run drain 2026-03-18 03:00 UTC; Anatoly will own telemetry extraction; Leila will own migration impact verification; I'll prepare RMA draft if escalation criteria hit.
leila_z: reporting: after drain, we should run a targeted memory stress test on that card with ECC diagnostics flag; if failures reproduce -> RMA.
anatoly_r: noted. I'll also attach a histogram of corrected-bit offsets to the incident ticket.
mike_h: thanks. tagging @oncall and ops: please standby.
infra-bot: acknowledged. scheduled job id: sched-4723. Reminder ping 30m before window.
leila_z: :thumbsup:
mike_h: closing loop: if anyone sees sudden Xid or reboot events before the window, call immediate page-retire full and evacuate the host.
leila_z: will do.
(ends)
